input: Read /doc/README.md and generate a table of contents from its headings (lines starting with # or ##). Insert the TOC after the first heading, formatted as a markdown list with '- [Heading Text](#anchor)' where anchor is the heading text lowercased with spaces replaced by hyphens. Write the result back to the file.

transcript.final_response:
I added the table of contents to `/doc/README.md`, right after the first heading (`# Project Alpha`), and saved the file.

It has one entry for each `#` and `##` heading:

```
- [Project Alpha](#project-alpha)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [API Reference](#api-reference)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
```

The first heading, "Project Alpha", is listed in the TOC alongside the others because it also starts with `#`. I didn't check that the links work. The anchors are just the heading text lowercased with spaces turned into hyphens, as you specified.
tool_calls:
cd /doc
toc=$(grep -E '^##? ' README.md | while IFS= read -r l; do
  t=$(echo "$l" | sed -E 's/^#+ +//')
  a=$(echo "$t" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr ' ' '-')
  echo "- [$t](#$a)"
done)
{ head -n 1 README.md; echo; echo "$toc"; tail -n +2 README.md; } > /tmp/new.md
cp /tmp/new.md README.md
cat README.md
